comparison: Both address viroplasm formation (C1, C2). OpenEval finds strong support from TEM and immunoelectron microscopy. Peer review (Reviewer #3) questions whether granules are truly viral P protein structures versus host stress granules, requesting additional immunoelectron microscopy despite data being provided (C2). Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

OpenEval R1 includes C3-C5 showing P protein scaffold role. Peer R2 addresses same claims (C3, C4, C5) and accepts these findings without challenge, agreeing P forms granules and recruits N and L proteins. Strong agreement on P's scaffold function.

Both evaluate LLPS evidence (C6-C9). OpenEval finds FRAP, fusion, and hexanediol data strongly support liquid-like properties. Peer review (Reviewer #2) raises significant concerns: FRAP normalization issues (actual recovery ~60% not 80%), hexanediol toxicity and non-specific effects on kinases/phosphatases. Major disagreement on data interpretation and sufficiency.

Both address ER association and actin-dependent movement (C10-C13). OpenEval finds strong support from time-lapse imaging and pharmacological inhibition. Peer reviewers accept these findings without critique. Complete agreement.

Both evaluate split-GFP data showing ER contact sites (C14-C15). OpenEval finds the proximity assay demonstrates nanoscale ER association. Peer reviewers accept this data without question. Complete agreement.

Both address biological relevance across hosts (C16-C17). OpenEval finds protoplast data supports generality. Peer review (Reviewer #3) requests demonstration in natural host barley using infectious clone or mini-replicon, questioning whether phase separation is adequately shown in natural infection context. Disagreement on sufficiency of protoplast evidence.

Both evaluate in vitro phase separation (C18-C23). OpenEval finds comprehensive evidence from multiple assays. Peer review (Reviewer #2) acknowledges authors 'conclusively demonstrate that P protein phase separates.' Strong agreement on intrinsic LLPS capacity.

Both address client recruitment into droplets (C24-C26). OpenEval finds N protein and RNA incorporation well-supported. Peer review (Reviewer #2) requests either softening the claim or providing full-length BYSMV RNA data, noting only 5' trailer sequence was used. Disagreement on scope of RNA recruitment claim.

Both evaluate phosphorylation mutant data (C27-C36). OpenEval finds extensive evidence from IDR prediction, mutant analysis, and biochemical fractionation strongly supports phosphorylation regulation. Peer review (Reviewer #2) accepts this as a strength: 'conclusively demonstrate that P protein phase separates and can be inhibited by CK1 kinase activity.' Strong agreement.

OpenEval R9 addresses CK1 overexpression effects (C37-C40), finding strong support. Peer R10 covers overlapping claims plus controls (C41-C45). While Reviewer #2 acknowledges CK1 data as strength, Reviewer #1 and essential revision #2 request genetic knockdown/knockout experiments, considering overexpression alone insufficient. Partial agreement with concerns about experimental completeness.

OpenEval R10 evaluates kinase-dead controls and phosphatase treatment (C41-C45), finding strong support for enzymatic specificity. Peer R10 includes these claims but requests additional genetic validation (knockdown/knockout). Agreement on control quality but disagreement on sufficiency without loss-of-function genetics.

Both evaluate minireplicon functional data (C46-C51) and regulatory model (C52-C54). OpenEval finds multiple complementary measurements support replication vs transcription switch. Peer review (Reviewer #2) finds minireplicon data 'confusing' and conclusions 'not as strongly supported,' requesting clarification or softening of claims. Reviewer #3 notes alternative explanations (decreased degradation vs increased biogenesis). Major disagreement on interpretation and strength of functional evidence.

OpenEval R12 synthesizes findings into regulatory model (C52-C54) linking phosphorylation-controlled phase separation to replication/transcription balance. Peer R11 addresses same model claims with significant skepticism, requesting data clarification and softer claims. Disagreement on whether convergent evidence sufficiently supports mechanistic model.
OpenEval evaluates novelty claim (C66) as uncertain due to dependence on literature scope and publication timeline. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific novelty claim.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic model (C72-C74) linking LLPS to differential N concentration requirements as uncertain/speculative, lacking direct evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluates ER-viroplasm functional interaction model (C77-C79) as uncertain, noting C78-C79 are speculative without direct evidence for molecular exchange or mRNA transport. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative claims.
